reason: H0 reaches the public vertex decoder with several strides, but its supplied OSS-Fuzz wiring performs an ordinary native CMake build and contains only explicit x86 cpuid-path manipulation. The changed logic is the WASM SIMD-specific wasmMoveMask implementation used by decodeBytesGroupSimd, so H0 provides no visible configuration that compiles or executes this production path. This is material because the new mask extraction uses lane multiplication by magic and depends on the stated 0xff/0x00 group invariant.
evidence: The only production change is inside SIMD_TARGET static void wasmMoveMask(v128_t mask, unsigned char& mask0, unsigned char& mask1).
The replacement computes mask0 and mask1 using wasm_i64x2_extract_lane(mask, ...) multiplied by the constant 0x000103070f1f3f80ull.
The source comment states that the constant assumes mask has 8 groups of 0xff or 0x00, exposing input-derived SIMD mask semantics worth fuzzing.
H0 calls meshopt_decodeVertexBuffer at strides 4, 16, 24, and 32, but does not select or emulate a WASM SIMD build.
H0's only implementation-path control is meshopt::cpuid = 0 under x86 architecture macros, which targets the scalar x86 fallback rather than wasmMoveMask.
build.sh runs cmake and make without any visible WASM or WASM SIMD toolchain/configuration.
recommended_action: Add a WASM SIMD build of the existing meshopt_decodeVertexBuffer fuzz target, execute it in a WASM-capable fuzzing setup, and retain inputs that exercise decodeBytesGroupSimd and wasmMoveMask across the supported vertex strides.
